newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks defy naysayers to end at 6-yr high.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks defy naysayers to end at 6-yr high.

text.p: Taiwan share prices rose on huge volume to another six-year high close on Tuesday, as more funds flew into the market in defiance of expected profit-taking and newly tightened margin-buying limits, brokers said.
Following a 135-point rise Monday, the benchmark stock index rose through the session to an intra-day high of 8,546.90 before closing at 8,526.20 -- a gain of 99.78 points or 1.18 percent.
The close surpassed a 8,182.44 finish of March 17 to mark the index's highest close since 8,569.55 on May 15, 1990.
Turnover was a huge T$183.645 billion, the highest in more than three years as investors said "no" to market naysayers.

"Investors were apparently fearless, unmoved by the newly trimmed margin-trading ratios, as they found their own way to get the funds they need to play in the red-hot bourse," said Oliver Fang of National Securities said.

Fang said a number of new faces, unable to resist the huge gains, withdrew time deposits at local banks to invest in the market, which has risen 24.7 percent in 1997 to become one of the best performing markets in the world.
Brokers estimated that some T$200 billion in new funds came from such withdrawals. Funds controlled by the government and ruling Nationalist Party also poured money in, they said.
With the significant exception of the electronics sector, which fell 0.16 percent, all sectors rose. Paper shares surged 3.65 percent, glass shares 2.42 percent and constructions 2.41.

Transport shares, which slipped at the opening, ended with a 0.3 percent rise as investors overcame the psychological impact of unconfirmed news reports of possible delays in plans to end a 48-year ban on direct Taiwan-China shipping.
Plans for a major new listing fuelled buying enthusiasm.
"A plan by EVA Airways, a unit of Evergreen Marine, to list in the market helped boost transport shares," said Fang of National Securities.
